title: US Energy Chief Exhorts Data Center Backers to Push Back Against Opponents
source_used: Business Insider (Africa edition) account of Chris Wright's remarks, 30 Jun 2026
key_facts: US Energy Secretary Chris Wright said at an Amazon Web Services conference on Tuesday that many data-center concerns are real but 'overblown'.
He urged supporters to push back on critics who cite environmental concerns and job losses: 'The pluses are way bigger than the minuses'.
He said more data centers are the path to lower-cost electricity and that water use is 'tiny' compared with their benefits.
He compared the debate with the anti-fracking campaign 15 years ago and said 'They cannot win, and they will not win' on the polls.
A Gallup survey of 1,000 US adults published in May found seven in ten opposed building AI data centers in their local area; nearly half were strongly opposed.
By the end of last year more than 1,400 US data centers had been built or approved, per Business Insider.
quote_evidence: "The pluses are way bigger than the minuses," he said.
A Gallup survey of 1,000 adults in the US published in May found that seven in 10 respondents opposed constructing data centers for AI in their local area.
why_it_matters_hint: The US energy chief is openly backing data-center builders against local opposition.
notes: OLD NEWS RE-DATED: EnergyNow URL is dated 2026/06. The EnergyNow headline matches a Reuters headline of 30 Jun; the text read is Business Insider's account of the same remarks. Reuters and EnergyNow pages blocked.
